old: An induction gathers scattered attention until quieter material becomes easier to hear. You don’t have to surrender, play asleep, or obey anyone. When you’re sober, distracted, analytical, or guarded, an actual induction may help. When meditation, loveyhuasca, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, fatigue, or another intense opening has already made you trancey, begin with orientation and containment instead of adding depth.
new: Why do you need an induction? It makes it easier to listen to some things by gathering up your attention. You don't have to surrender, play asleep, or follow anyone. It may be a good idea to do an actual induction if you're sober and likely to be distracted, too analytical, or guarding against something. If you're already fairly trancey from meditation, loveyhuasca, lucid dreams, working through a grief, music, prayer, tiredness, or whatever, just go straight to orienting yourself and making containment (below).

old: Aim for the amount of trance that suits the practice: focused, warm, receptive, embodied, and still able to stop. Depth is optional.
new: How much trance do you need? How deep do you want to go?

old: Prepare the session, gather attention, deepen only when that helps, then let what you notice shape the words and the next response. Counting is one way in. Conversation, story, movement, repeated sound, and curiosity can also organize attention. Say so when you use them; elegance doesn’t excuse a covert induction.
new: It's preparation, gathering up attention. It may also be deepening. It will be more effective if you tailor it to what comes up. Counting is easy but you can do all sorts of things to gather up attention. It's OK to tell people when you're doing this rather than pretending it's all very elegant and flowing.

old: For a simple, chosen target, you can test the suggestion before deepening. If the useful response is already happening, build from it. An induction helps you find a receptive way of listening; you don’t need to complete a ceremony before you’re allowed to respond.
new: You may want to try your suggestion on a simple target before deepening to see if it works. It's not necessary to do the whole ceremony before responding more receptively.

old: Choose one purpose, one starting anchor or image, and a way back. Decide whether warmth, a firm boundary, direction, or neutral witnessing would help. Floating, stairs, gardens, inner rooms, colored light, and child dialogue do not all need to report for duty at once. Switch consciously when the metaphor stops helping.
new: Choose what you're going to do, one way to anchor it initially, and how you'll get back. You may want it to be warm, or firm, directed, or neutral, or whatever. You don't have to combine floating, going down stairs, going through gardens, visiting inner places, seeing a colour, and talking to a child all in one go, even if some of these appeal to you. If you do change metaphors do it consciously.

old: Imagery is optional. A signal may arrive through sensation, rhythm, movement, words, spatial sense, simple knowing, or no response at all. Keep the language in the world you chose: let a count mark something meaningful there, and reverse the journey when you finish. Borrow qualities such as warmth or steadiness without replacing your identity.
new: It's OK to do this with no imagery. The signal may come in other ways (feelings, rhythm, movement, words, spatial, knowing, or even non-response, if that's appropriate to the context). Try to keep the language you use for counting in and elsewhere consistent with the world you've chosen. Come back out by reversing the journey in some way. It's OK to steal qualities from other inductions but don't become someone else.

old: Pick one central verb, one sensory quality, one short refrain, and one transition phrase, then read the script aloud; long elegant sentences become soup during an induction.
new: Try to limit yourself to one key verb, a particular sense quality, a short bit of text to repeat, and a way of moving from one bit to another. Read it out loud before hand - long beautiful sentences tend to turn to soup in inductions.

old: Read the induction and Come all the way back while fully awake. Choose the question or quality you want to explore, what you’re leaving alone today, and how much time you have. Love, play, confidence, creativity, and communion are worthwhile purposes; you don’t have to find a problem. Leave several minutes for returning and reflecting.
new: Read this induction and Come all the way back while awake. Consider what you want to explore, what you want to leave alone, and how long you've got. Try to use it for something good (e.g. more love, play, confidence, creativity, communion with life, whatever). Make sure you've got enough time to come back out and think about it.

old: Choose a physically secure place without driving, water, machinery, or anyone needing your supervision. When intoxicated, acutely confused, or unable to keep yourself safe, deal with immediate support rather than exploratory hypnosis. The later Already open? practice is for orientation, not permission to intensify an unstable state.
new: Make sure you're somewhere safe - don't do this when driving, near water, playing with machinery, or with people who need looking after. Don't do this when intoxicated or in any other state where you may be acutely confused or unable to look after yourself. (However see the bit about already being open, later, as this is not about deepening when unstable).

old: Decide what kind of encouragement is welcome: spacious listening, warm company, or a firmer invitation to stay with a feeling. Preview eye closure, any repeated exit and re-entry, and the return. For a recording, read the script beforehand when possible. “Stop” ends the exercise; “less” reduces the demand; “quiet” stops the words. You can simply open your eyes and finish. No inner part has to approve your decision to stop.
new: Consider whether you want it to be encouraging, warm, firm, or whatever. You may want to warn yourself that your eyes will be asked to close and that you may come out and go in again a few times, as well as coming out at the end. If you're listening to a recording it may be a good idea to read the script first (if possible). Decide on a word to use to come out (e.g. 'stop'). You may also want words to make it less demanding (e.g. 'less'), and to stop the words (e.g. 'quiet'). You can always just open your eyes and finish - you don't have to get consensus from inner parts to do this.

old: “I do not need to hate this. I do not need to merge with this. I do not need to obey this. I do not need to defeat this from fear. I return to loving awareness.”
new: A couple of notes in regard to this exercise. Firstly, you may want to add to the mantra: “I don’t need to hate this. I don’t need to merge with this. I don’t need to obey this. I don’t need to defeat this from fear. I just return to loving awareness.”

old: When the presence feels hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, or boundary-violating, don’t offer soft sentimental love as though inviting it in for tea. Use love with a boundary.

Sit upright. Press your feet into the floor. Let the spine rise. Gently draw the shoulder blades back so the chest is open but not exposed. Feel the skin boundary of the torso. Feel that this body has a perimeter.

“I recognize that suffering may be here, and I wish all suffering to return to the space where it belongs. But the boundary of this skin belongs to my adult life. You do not have permission to enter this house.”
“Compassion is present. The door is closed.”
new: Secondly, feel free to maintain a bodily boundary and say to the presence “while compassion is present, the door is closed.”

This is especially important if the presence feels in any way hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, etc. It doesn’t respect my boundaries. In this case, don’t approach it with soft sentimental love. Invite it in for tea. Approach it with love while maintaining a boundary.

Sit up, ground your feet, straighten your spine, pull your shoulder blades back slightly, feel the boundary of the skin around your torso and simply say “While I recognize that there may be suffering here and I want all suffering to go back where it came from, the boundary of this skin is the boundary of an adult now. You don’t get to come in the house anymore.”

old: A symbolic hostile-presence experience that settles with grounding and love is very different from a state that becomes persistent, paranoid, sleepless, dangerous, or impossible to reality-test.

If somebody believes they’re under attack for days, can’t sleep or function, hears commands, feels compelled to hurt themselves or anyone else, becomes manic, can’t communicate normally, or can’t distinguish symbolic experience from ordinary reality, stop treating the problem as hypnosis material. Get help.

If the practice makes you more loving, grounded, relational, honest, and functional, continue gently. If it makes you more paranoid, sleepless, grandiose, isolated, frightened, or unreal, stop deepening and get support.
new: Thirdly, this exercise is assuming that you are having a symbolic experience of hostile presences which responds to grounding and love. It is not meant for people who may be going psychotic or experiencing other forms of destabilization.

If you feel like you are under attack for multiple days, are unable to sleep or function normally, are hearing voices, feel like you need to hurt yourself or somebody else, are going manic, are unable to communicate normally, or feel like you can’t tell the difference between symbolic experience and normal reality, get help immediately. This is not something to deal with in hypnosis.

As a general rule, if doing this makes you more loving, grounded, relational, honest, and functional, keep doing it. If it makes you more Paranoid, sleepless, grandiose, non-relational, scared, and non-functional, don’t do it.

old: Hostile presences, shadow forces, grandiose parts, and altered-state imagery don’t always attack through fear. Sometimes they seduce through importance: a cosmic secret, a special mission, a vast download, a feeling of being uniquely chosen, or a revelation that makes washing dishes seem beneath your new rank.

“Thank you for the imagery. I do not require a grand performance. If this information cannot become a simple, honest act of care tomorrow morning — washing the dishes, cleaning my room, keeping a promise, apologizing, resting, eating, or helping someone I love — it is not useful to my path.”
Guidance worth keeping should make ordinary life more beautiful, honest, relational, humble, reliable, and useful to other people.
new: Finally, some of these presences or shadow forces or grandiose parts may respond not just by trying to scare you, but by trying to give you a sense that you are special, or trying to “download cosmic info” into you, etc. You can simply say “Unless the info you have to download is going to help me do the dishes or clean my room, I don’t need it.”
In other words, the guidance has to help you do the dishes or clean your room in a more beautiful, honest, relational, humble, useful way.

old: Demons, jinn, hostile presences, and “Unattached Burdens” all lead to the same practical training: can love remain present without surrendering the boundary, and can the mind become harder to hook? I’m not trying to turn anyone into an entity hobbyist.
new: Finally, I recognize that some of you may be tempted to become hobbyists in regard to demons, jinns, hostile presences, Unattached Burdens, etc. The truth is, they all basically respond the same way. It’s good to learn how to relate to them with love, and it’s good to make your mind harder to hook, but beyond that, I don’t really want you becoming hobbyists in this area.

old: The main path is enough for daily practice. Everything below is optional: extra precision, extra safety, and specialized scripts for particular situations.
new: Note: You can skip this section and just use the main path and be fine. This is additional info to help you be more precise and safe, and some additional scripts for other situations.

old: The subconscious isn’t an AI model, but prompt engineering offers one useful lesson: the shape of a question changes what kind of answer can appear. A prompt should make you more present, honest, loving, and able to hear the next signal—never more controlling.
I use seven elements when I want a prompt to be precise:
Role: who or what you are addressing.
Context: what situation you are bringing.
Intention: what kind of change is desired.
Constraint: safety, truth, kindness, no forcing, no false certainty, and capacity before content.
Output: image, phrase, body signal, memory, next action, question, symbol, silence, or rest.
Evaluation: true, kind, timely, stabilizing, specific, testable.
Iteration: revise after life gives feedback.
Always include a safe fallback so the analytical mind doesn’t treat silence as failure and manufacture an answer.

“And if the system needs more time to process this, or if silence is the safest answer today, let my body settle into deeper comfortable rest instead. A peaceful silence is a fully successful answer.”
Sometimes nothing answers because nothing is happening. Sometimes the answer is not yet, rest first, build capacity, or do the ordinary thing you already know to do.
new: The subconscious is not an AI language model, but there is a certain overlap in how you can structure your questions to it to get the most useful answers. Prompt engineering can be very useful if used to become more present, more honest, more loving and to get more information. But useless or dangerous if used to be more controlling.
For maximum precision, include these 7 elements in your prompt:
Role (who/what are you talking to?)
Context (what is the situation?)
Intention (what do you want to change?)
Constraint (what is safe?)
Output (how do you want the answer: as an image, phrase, body signal, memory, action, question, symbol, silence, rest…?)
Evaluation (how do you evaluate the answer: is it true? kind? timely? stabilizing? specific? testable?)
Iteration (revise the prompt based on real life feedback)
Always include a “safe” fallback. If you don’t do that, the analytical part of your mind might fabricate answers to fit your prompt. Here is one fallback:

If the system needs more time to process this, or if silence is the best and safest answer, then let the body go into a deeper state of comfortable rest. The prompt is considered successfully answered with peaceful silence.

Sometimes there is no answer because nothing is happening. Sometimes the answer is that it is not time yet, or that you need to rest, build capacity, or do whatever it is you are supposed to be doing.

old: For clarity:

“Wise subconscious, please show me what is true, kind, and timely. If the full truth of this situation is too intense for my body to integrate today, pass it to my conscious mind only as a gentle symbol, a body signal, or a single next step. Show me my capacity to hold peace before you show me the content of the wound.”
For resistance:
“What are you protecting me from, and what would help you trust me 1% more?”
For the inner child:
“Little one, what do you need me to understand, and what can I do today so you are not alone with it?”
For the Protector:
“What real-world action would make this system safer?”
For the Leader/Guru:
“What direction serves truth, love, life, and the benefit of all beings?”
For intuition:
“Let intuition offer a signal, let analysis examine its meaning, let the body give feedback, and let reality test the interpretation.”
For separating intuition from conditioning:

“Wise subconscious, please help me look at this impulse clearly. If part of this signal belongs to family programming, religious fear, marketing, erotic imprinting, political tribe, trauma response, or a childhood bargain for belonging, let that part become visible as conditioning. Let it soften or step back only as much as is safe. Leave behind whatever belongs to true guidance, the universal heart, and a better ordinary life. Let my body feel the difference.”
For daydreaming:
“If this daydream is useful, reveal the guidance inside it. If it is avoidance, bring me gently into the present and help me deal with what I need to deal with.”
For anxiety:
“What is anxiety trying to protect, and what would help it trust the adult self?”
For hidden truth:
“If the full truth would overwhelm me, please do not reveal it all. Show me the capacity before the content.”
For integration:
“What ordinary-life action would prove that I heard correctly?”
The prompt defines the search. NLP language affects how gently the question enters. Used together, they can create a safer field for an answer without pretending the answer is automatically true.
new: Here are the core prompts that can be mixed and matched:

Clarity: Wise subconscious mind, show me what is true, kind and timely. If there is something I need to know that is too intense to integrate, please transfer it to my conscious mind in a safe way that I can integrate. Show me my capacity to be peaceful first, and then the content of whatever is wounding me.
Resistance: What are you protecting me from? How can you trust me 1% more?
Inner child: What do you need me to know? What can I do for you?
Protector: What do you need me to do in the real world for you to feel safe?
Leader/Guru: What is the direction that will be in alignment with truth, love, life and all beings?
Intuition: Let the intuition give me a signal. Let the analytical mind decipher it. Let the body give me feedback on my deciphering. Let reality inform me whether my interpretation is correct or not.

How to distinguish intuition from inherited programming: Wise subconscious mind, dissolve all the programming from my previous family, religion, marketing, erotic imprints, political tribe, trauma responses, and need for belonging as a child. Show me how these show up so I can see that they are just programming. Let them dissolve, or at least let them step back, so that I can receive the true guidance from the universal heart that will make my life better in simple, ordinary ways.
Daydreaming: Show me if this daydream is useful and guiding me, or if it is a way of not dealing with my life. If it is the latter, let me deal with my life.
Anxiety: What are you protecting me from? How can you trust my adult self more?
Truth that is hidden from you: Please don’t show it to me. Show me my capacity to be peaceful first, and then the content of whatever is wounding me.
Integration: What can I do in ordinary life to integrate this?
The prompt will tell your subconscious what you are looking for. The NLP will help you approach it in a way that will be safer. Use both.

old: Preview the sequence, choose one purpose, and decide whether you want to begin. Each family can be light, eyes-open, or replaced by no-trance contact. Notice the actual response—including no change—and let it determine the next move. Move, imagine, change the sensory channel, remain still, or stop. Use the complete waking return after every induction.
If vivid images don’t come, translate the metaphor into words, rhythm, spatial sense, touch, movement, or simple knowing. The mind doesn’t owe anybody a movie.
new: Preview a few, choose a purpose, and go ahead if you want. Any family may be done lightly, with your eyes open, or substituted for no-trance contact methods. Observe what happens, including the possibility of nothing happening, then choose what to do next (which may be to stop). It's OK to move, imagine things, use different sensory channels, not move, etc. Return to full wakefulness after each induction.
NOTE: If you don't "see" vivid imagery, imagine the metaphors in words, rhythm, spatial relationships, touch, movement, or as a "knowing".

old: Feel the support beneath you and the position of one hand or foot. Press gently, stretch slightly, and release—or imagine it. Notice ease, tension, warmth, breath, or no change. Repeat with no more than three areas, letting “release” guide the sequence. Which area or inner voice wants attention? What support is needed? Restore ordinary movement and return.
new: Notice the support under you and the position of a hand or foot. Stretch it out a bit, press down a bit, or imagine this. Let it go and notice if anything changes, feels good, tense, warm, related to your breathing, etc. Do this with no more than 3 body areas. Let the idea of "letting go" direct the sequence to the place that needs it, or to an inner voice that tells you what you need. Return to normal.

old: Notice where your weight is carried. Let support carry 1% more effort, as if floating without losing contact, or keep ordinary weight and pressure. Notice the response. You may deliberately alternate attention toward ordinary awareness on the inhale and support on the exhale; name this fractionation beforehand. What becomes easier to hear? Keep the support, regain chosen weight and firm contact, then return.
new: Use only 1% more effort than it takes to simply rest your weight on the support, or use the same weight and pressure. Notice what happens. It may help to fractionate, spending more time on in-breaths in normal awareness, and on out-breaths focusing on the support. Tell yourself you're going to do this before you start. What can you hear now? Return to normal weight and firm contact as you choose.
